title: Service registry: GPU capability signals and routing strategy
body:
TL;DR:
This doc proposes a practical schema and control-plane behaviour for a global service registry focused on GPU capability discovery, continuous health signals, and routing policy hooks for multi-region LLM inference. Goals: let routing pick best compatible hosts by GPU type, availability, and health; enable graceful fallbacks across model variants; keep control-plane cheap and eventually shippable to Dedicated/Private deployments.

Context and constraints:
- Our serving runtime needs to choose targets by: GPU architecture (A100/H100 variants), memory capacity, compute class (FP32/FP16/INT8 support), and node-level health.
- Many consumers will request for model variants (e.g. gptx-4-8k-quant) that require certain hardware features.
- The registry must be friendly to hosted API (real-time routing) and to Dedicated/Private (local registries, eventual sync).
- We must avoid very chatty control-plane traffic; prefer push heartbeats with compact deltas and incremental state sync for control-plane consumers.

Scope of this doc:
- Registry entry schema (canonical fields we will emit from agent/host agents).
- Label taxonomy and GPU capability vocabulary (canonical strings).
- Health signals and sampling cadence + scoring model for routing decisions.
- Control-plane responsibilities: leader election, eventual consistency, and multi-region hints.
- Routing policy hooks: cost/latency/compatibility/fallthrough.
- Rollout notes and open questions.

Registry entry (canonical, flattened):
- id: host-uuid-1234 (string)
- region: us-west1 (string)
- zone: us-west1-b (string)
- hostname: rwd-inf-gpu-023.internal (string)
- ip: 10.12.3.45 (string)
- labels: ["gpu:h100-platine","rack:r12","env:prod"] (list of strings)
- gpu_types: ["H100-80GB","A100-40GB"] (list of strings)
- cpu_cores: "64" (string)
- total_gpu_count: "4" (string)
- free_gpu_count: "2" (string)
- memory_gb: "1024" (string)
- capacity_score: "0.73" (string; 0..1 computed locally)
- last_heartbeat: "2026-02-20T14:32:02Z" (string)
- health_signals: ["temp_celsius:73","gpu_mem_util_pct:42","uct_latency_ms:18"] (list of strings)
- compat_tags: ["int8:yes","fp16:yes","sparse_attention:partial"] (list of strings)
- maintenance_windows: ["2026-02-22T01:00Z/2026-02-22T04:00Z"] (list of strings)
- metadata: ["kube_node:gpu-pool-3","owner:serving-team"] (list of strings)

Why flattened lists: makes incremental delta sync easy via vector diffs and avoids nesting when writing to lightweight KV stores.

Label taxonomy (principles):
- Labels SHOULD be short, lower-case, colon-separated key:value pairs.
- Avoid free-form descriptions; use a small controlled vocabulary for gpu types and compat flags.
- Two orthogonal label sets: static (hardware, rack, region) and dynamic (load, maintenance, taints).
- Static example keys: gpu, rack, rev, network-class. Dynamic keys: taint, in_maintenance, free_gpus.

Canonical GPU vocabulary (initial set):
- H100-80GB -> "h100-80"
- H100-94GB -> "h100-94"
- A100-40GB -> "a100-40"
- L40s -> "l40s"
Also keep an alias map in control-plane to map cloud provider SKU names to our canonical strings.

Health signals and how routing uses them:
- Heartbeat cadence: default 10s from host agent. If hosts are behind NAT or constrained environments, allow 30s.
- Signals to collect (minimal): last_heartbeat, gpu_mem_util_pct, gpu_temp_celsius, pcie_error_rate, process_count, tail_latency_99_ms (for local queues).
- Compute a single node_health_score in host agent using an exponential-weighted average (EWA) of recent signals: 0 (unhealthy) .. 1 (green). This is what routing reads first.
- We keep a short history window (5m) in the control-plane for health-trend detection (regressions).
- Example thresholds to mark node as degraded: gpu_temp_celsius > 85 for >120s OR gpu_mem_util_pct > 92% steady for 3 samples OR pcie_error_rate spikes above baseline * 3.

Capacity and capability negotiation:
- Consumer supplies: required_compat_tags (list), min_free_gpus (int), prefer_region (list), max_acceptable_latency_ms (int).
- Registry consumer does a two-step selection: (1) narrow by compat_tags + region + taints, (2) score by composite (latency_estimate, capacity_score, cost_tier, health_score).
- Score examples: score = w1*(1 - latency_norm) + w2*capacity_score + w3*health_score - w4*cost_tier. We will start with weights (0.4, 0.25, 0.25, 0.1). Tunable in Console.

Routing policies and fallbacks:
- Policy: prefer-local-region -> if none healthy, cross-region -> if none with compat, degrade to quantized-variant (if allow_lower_quality=true) -> finally queue/retry.
- Canary and A/B routing: control-plane tags a small % of traffic with preferred routing hints (route_hint: experimental-pool) for rollout.
- Graceful fallback: when route picks a node that reports a runtime incompatibility (rare), runtime returns a well-known status "incompatible_capability" and route engine attempts next candidate immediately. This keeps RTT reasonable.

Control-plane design notes:
- Architecture: regional control-plane replicas (read-optimized local cache) + central leader for authoritative writes (model updates, label schema).
- Sync: hosts push heartbeats to local regional control-plane endpoint; regional replicas publish compact deltas via change-log (replicated to central).
- Consistency: relaxed consistency for routing decisions is OK; strong consistency for label schema updates and global taints. Use causal timestamps for important writes.
- Scale: expected ~100k host entries in global registry at scale; use sharded indexes by region and gpu_type for fast lookup.

Multi-region considerations:
- Locality: route engine should prefer local replica reads for latency; central decides cross-region fallback policies and publishes them to replicas as config.
- Traffic shaping: when a region is degraded, control-plane increases remote pool weights gradually to avoid capacity shock.
- Cost controls: provide per-customer routing knobs to avoid unbounded egress/cross-region costs.

Operational signals and observability:
- Expose per-route telemetry: selected_host, score_breakdown, health_before_select, fallback_reason. Surface in Console and per-request trace id.
- Alerts: region-level degraded if >10% hosts have health_score < 0.4 for 5m. Node-level sale: 3 consecutive missed heartbeats -> mark stale; 6 -> remove from routing pool.
- Audit log: all routing decisions that cross-account boundaries need audit entries for compliance.

Edge cases / private deployments:
- Private deployments may have single-region: allow a config flag to disable cross-region fallback and require explicit admin override.
- Air-gapped envs: registry can run as a pull model where control-plane posts signed bundles to a secure artifact store and local agents pull.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Pilot: implement host agent and registry schema in two regions; run internal serving workloads with non-critical models. Collect health metrics and tune thresholds (4 weeks).
2) Beta: enable routing hooks for a subset of customer traffic with canary fallback. Add Console knobs for weights. (6 weeks).
3) GA: promote to default routing for hosted API and expose configs to Dedicated customers. Add private deployment packaging. (8-12 weeks).

Security and compliance notes:
- Heartbeats and registry writes must be authenticated with mTLS and short-lived credentials.
- Sensitive metadata fields must be opt-in; avoid leaking rack or physical location unless necessary for routing.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is the right default heartbeat cadence for high-density GPU farms? (10s seems OK but costs need measurement).
- Decide canonical cost_tier values and how they map to pricing units.
- Finalize alias map from cloud SKUs -> our GPU vocabulary. Add tests for every new SKU.
- Decide retention window for control-plane short-term history (5m vs 15m).

Notes / references:
- Related tickets: JIRA-PLAT-1423 (registry schema), JIRA-SERV-2101 (routing fallbacks), GH-987 (agent -> registry proto).
- Slack: #infra-service-registry for quick sync; recommend a short RFC before merging schema changes.

Appendix: quick checklist for host-agent implementer:
- emit flattened fields listed above every heartbeat; include delta encoding when possible.
- compute local node_health_score using the EWA formula (coeffs TBD).
- include compat_tags and advertise quantized/packed model support explicitly.
- implement fast rejection header for incompatible models to keep client latency low.

If you want, I can convert this into a condensed RFC email or a Confluence-ready page. For the next step I propose a short spike to instrument cost of 10s vs 30s heartbeat on a 1k-host cluster and a proof-of-concept route engine that demonstrates the score breakdown in traces.
